mechanism_narrative: The continued improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and the smaller decline in RETAIL_REC signal broadening out-of-home activity, which should lift retail footfall further over the next four weeks as consumers make more linked shopping trips.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to recover but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain depressed, discretionary shopping shifts toward local errands and nearby retail, so RETAIL_REC rises within one to two weeks after each additional week of home-centered mobility.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -30 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +20
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 and WORKPLACES stays below -30 for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its current depressed level would reduce access to high-street retail and suppress shopping trips, causing RETAIL_REC to fall within the next week.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -40 but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the same or following week, the signal is false.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS mobility draws activity toward outdoor leisure instead of shopping destinations, so retail-and-recreation mobility weakens over the next four weeks if park visits continue to rise from the current trough.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks from below -30
failure_condition: If PARKS rises for two straight weeks from below -30 yet RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a rebound in WORKPLACES and only modest weakness in TRANSIT indicates more normal weekday circulation, which should lift retail visits within two to four weeks as commute-linked shopping returns.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while TRANSIT is no worse than -40
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises for two weeks and TRANSIT stays above -40 but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM approaches baseline, routine essential trips stabilize household movement patterns and spill over into nearby discretionary shopping, producing a near-term rise in RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5 but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The retail rebound stalls if mobility restrictions intensify and workplace attendance falls again, because reduced daily mixing cuts spontaneous shopping trips and short-horizon retail activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops below -35 and TRANSIT remains below -38
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES drops below -35 and TRANSIT remains below -38 but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In summer leisure conditions, continued weakness in PARKS paired with stable or improving TRANSIT implies households are not reallocating time to outdoor venues, so retail mobility should edge up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS remains below -25 and TRANSIT does not worsen, yet RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
